overview: The Kronenwetter Village Board held a special meeting on August 27, 2026, with one primary action item: accepting the resignation of Village Clerk Jennifer Poyer, which passed 6-0. The meeting was preceded by pointed public comment from three residents criticizing the board over two costly workplace investigations totaling $105,000, vague closed session notices, and broader governance concerns. Trustee Stowell was absent.
committee: Village of Kronenwetter Special Village Board Meeting

agenda.item: New Business - Acceptance of Clerk's Resignation

discussions.body: Three residents spoke critically of the village board. Bruny Kramer of 2150 E. State Hwy 153 criticized a pattern of poor governance over the past six months, referencing a mining situation and excessive closed sessions, and suggested board members seek training. Chris Johnson of 1998 Woodgate Lane delivered an extended rebuke, alleging that a workplace investigation costing approximately $40,000 was rooted in ego between President Joling and former administrator Sorenson, that closed session notices were improperly vague, and that employee privacy was mishandled through inadequate redactions; Johnson also addressed an apparent comment made about her Facebook posts before the meeting, calling it unprofessional. Guy Fredl of 2240 Ruby Drive, identifying himself as a longtime village volunteer, presented specific cost figures—$60,000 for a first investigation by Von Briesen and Roper and $45,000 for a second, totaling $105,000—and noted the village had lost three employees and three female board members in recent years, warning of potential litigation from Peter Wagner and Jennifer Poyer and suggesting the village hire a contracted HR professional to handle such matters.

The board voted 6-0 to accept the resignation of Village Clerk Jennifer Poyer as submitted. Following the vote, a trustee—identified in the transcript as raising additional comments—asked that staff coordinate a transition plan covering return of village property, system and social media passwords, and a status report from Poyer on outstanding work items. The same trustee thanked Poyer for her work on community events, social media, and elections, and wished her well. President Joling noted the village may need to call an additional meeting if an interim clerk is secured.

publicComment: Three residents offered public comment. Bruny Kramer (2150 E. State Hwy 153) criticized the board's governance over six months, citing the mining situation and closed sessions, and suggested board members attend seminars on proper governance. Chris Johnson (1998 Woodgate Lane) challenged the administrator's characterization that she 'hates the village,' disputed legal explanations for delays in releasing an investigation report, alleged the $40,000-plus investigation was driven by ego rather than necessity, and criticized overly vague closed session notices and inadequate redactions that failed to protect staff. Guy Fredl (2240 Ruby Drive), a longtime village volunteer, cited $105,000 in total investigation costs across two outside law firm engagements, noted loss of three employees and three female board members, warned of potential state and civil litigation from Wagner and Poyer, and recommended the village retain a contracted HR professional.
actionItems: Staff to develop a coordinated transition plan for the clerk position, including return of village property and transfer of system, program, and social media passwords
Outgoing clerk Jennifer Poyer requested (though not required) to provide a status report on outstanding work items
Board may convene an additional special meeting if an interim clerk arrangement is reached

votes.item: Acceptance of Village Clerk's resignation as submitted
votes.motion: Motion to accept the resignation of the employee as submitted to the board
